Quick notes / authoritative defaults (draft):

1) Definitions (concise):
- Raw prompts: the exact textual content submitted by users (user-provided prompt text).
- Model outputs: the generated text returned by the model for that request.
- Request/response metadata: headers, latencies, token counts, model id, route id, and anonymized error traces used for debugging.

2) Default retention (hosted API — Redwood-managed):
- Raw prompts: 30 days (kept to enable quick debugging and short-term quality monitoring).
- Model outputs: 30 days (paired with prompts for triage).
- Request/response metadata (telemetry): 365 days for aggregated metrics; raw telemetry for debugging (traces, full request/response logs) retained 90 days.

3) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Defaults align with hosted unless customer requests stricter policies at contract time. We offer a 90-day or 30-day retention SLA in agreements; by default we keep prompts/outputs 30 days unless contracted otherwise. Telemetry retention options are configurable.

4) Private (VPC/on-prem):
- By default, data does not leave the customer's VPC; Redwood-managed control plane retains only control metadata. Retention windows are customer-controlled — default installation manifests include a 0-day retention for raw prompts/outputs in our examples but can be configured.

5) Deletion / purge details & caveats:
- On a customer deletion request we remove primary copies within the stated window (typically 30 days for hosted). Backups and cold snapshots may be removed on a 7–30 day cycle depending on backup cadence — we include this caveat in responses.
- Legal holds: we cannot purge data subject to a lawful hold; we surface this in the questionnaire text.
- Redaction: customers can opt-in to automatic prompt redaction (hash-only storage) for PII-sensitive workloads; this reduces retention surface.

6) Residency / encryption / access controls:
- Hosted: we store data in the region selected at signup; encryption at rest and in transit is standard.
- Dedicated/Private: customer selects region and key controls (KMS/HSM).

7) Short customer-friendly bullet for reply to Acme (single paragraph):
"By default on our hosted service we retain raw prompts and model outputs for 30 days (used for short-term debugging and quality monitoring). Request/response telemetry used for operational monitoring is retained longer (raw debug logs 90 days; aggregated metrics up to 365 days). Dedicated deployments can be contracted for shorter SLAs; Private deployments keep data in your VPC and retention is under your control. We offer redaction and immediate purge options, but note that backups and legal holds can extend removal timelines."

If that looks good I can rephrase for Sam and attach the short retention table.

Short answer (copyable):
"For our hosted API, we treat the following as \"logs\": raw prompts (user-submitted text), model outputs, and request/response metadata. Default hosted retention: raw prompts & model outputs are retained for 30 days; raw debug logs (full request/response traces) for operational triage are retained 90 days; aggregated telemetry used for product/usage analytics is retained up to 365 days. Dedicated customers can request shorter retention in contract; Private/VPC deployments keep data in-customer-control and retention is configurable by the customer. Customers may also opt into prompt redaction or request immediate purge — note that backups and legal holds may delay full removal.
